name: listbox
title: Listbox
purpose: A list of options, always in view, from which the reader selects one or several.
whenToUse: To choose one or several of a known set where the reader benefits from seeing the options and a fact about each, such as branches with how far ahead they are.
As the list of results under a search field, or inside a popover opened from a button that shows the current choice.
With groups when the options fall into a few named sets.
whenNotToUse: In a form that must work with no script. Use a select, radios or checkboxes: a listbox needs the app's keyboard handling.
For two to four short options that fit a row. Use a segmented control or radios.
For a list of actions. Use a menu.
For rows that navigate. Use a list of links.
For filters above a list. Use filter chips.

variants.name: single-select
variants.use: The default. Exactly one option carries aria-selected="true".

variants.name: multi-select
variants.use: Add aria-multiselectable="true" to the listbox. Any number of options carry aria-selected="true". There is no modifier class.

variants.name: grouped
variants.use: Options inside ds-listbox__group elements, each with a ds-listbox__label.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: Each option is at least 44px tall and as wide as the listbox.

accessibility: Use a div with the class ds-listbox and role="listbox", named by aria-labelledby pointing at its visible label or by aria-label. Add aria-multiselectable="true" when several options may be selected.

Each option is a div with ds-listbox__option, role="option", an id and aria-selected set to "true" or "false" on every option. The check is drawn by the stylesheet from aria-selected, in a slot every row keeps.
A group is a div with ds-listbox__group, role="group" and aria-labelledby pointing at its ds-listbox__label, which carries role="presentation".

Trailing text goes in a span with ds-listbox__meta and is part of the option's name. An option that cannot be chosen carries aria-disabled="true", stays in the arrow-key order, and gives its reason in that trailing text.

The keyboard contract is the app's. Focus is roving: exactly one option has tabindex="0", the selected one or else the first, and every other option has tabindex="-1", so Tab enters and leaves the listbox in one stop.

Down and Up move focus to the next and the previous option and stop at the ends. Home and End go to the first and the last. A typed letter moves to the next option that starts with it. On each move the app swaps the tabindex values and calls focus() on the option.
In a single-select listbox, Space or Enter selects the focused option, or selection follows focus where selecting has no side effect. The app sets aria-selected="true" on it and "false" on the rest.

In a multi-select listbox, Space switches the focused option, Shift with Down or Up switches the option moved to, and Ctrl or Cmd with A selects all. A press on an option does the same as Space on it. The app ignores presses on an option with aria-disabled="true".

With no options, loading or after a failed load, keep the ds-listbox box without role="listbox" and put one ds-listbox__note in it: a sentence with role="status" that says what to try, a spinner with its text, or a sentence with role="alert" and a button that loads again. An element with role="listbox" always holds at least one option.
